per_policy_guidance.guidance: Low-confidence red-centered specialist, not a routine default. In the fixed in-distribution protocol it passed 4/12 runs. Invoke only from its supported state: drawer_position strictly >0.26 m, red exposed, and a reliable current red pose, with entry at the drawer front or during red approach/contact/lift. Its red-frame representation is intended for red-pose displacement, but no displaced-red validation exists. Avoid after red release, when blue/post-release geometry dominates, when the red pose is stale, or when transformed targets may be obstructed/unreachable. Treat lack of red/TCP co-motion after closing, IK non-convergence, low carried-red motion into furniture, red outside the pad or following retreat, or drawer_position falling to <=0.26 as failure. Validation failures ended either with red off-pad (5 runs) or red on-pad but the drawer below threshold (3 runs); several had hundreds of unconverged IK steps. Three failed runs transiently met the exit rule and later lost it, so verify the fixed condition at handoff rather than accepting a transient pass. Handoff: require red contained on the pad and no longer following TCP while drawer_position remains >0.26; the retained overlap can continue into blue pickup, with observed blue/TCP co-motion on initial lift as the cleanest cue to switch to blue_insert.

Preferred default among these policies when phase confidence is low and the state matches the demonstrated segment entry. It passed 10/12 in-distribution runs, with zero reported unconverged IK steps in all 12. Use with drawer_position >0.26 m, red visible and preferably acquired or in a demonstrated-style approach, and a current reachable red_goal. The destination-centered representation is intended for pad-relative placement; relocated-pad benefit is not validated. Avoid using it as the assumed solution to a far-displaced red pickup, blue displacement, obstruction, or unreachable goal. The two validation failures kept the drawer open (final 0.2935 and 0.2943 m) but left red off-pad, so an open drawer and clean IK are insufficient: monitor red support/containment, opening before support, red following retreat, and stale blue targeting. Handoff: confirm red is on the pad, no longer follows TCP, and drawer_position is still >0.26. Its supervised overlap can be handed to blue_insert while red is still held/touching because release context is included; established blue/TCP co-motion during initial lift is the least ambiguous nominal switch cue.

Use for represented intermediate entries or red-versus-blue phase ambiguity only when the caller can infer the semantic phase from current geometry. It passed 9/12 in-distribution runs. Require drawer_position >0.26 m and select: drawer_release_to_red before red contact; red_grasp_transport_place while closing/carrying/descending red; red_release_to_blue after supported release and during transit; blue_pickup for blue approach/closure/lift. Avoid guessing the phase, and do not assume this local-TCP representation handles large red/goal displacement. Wrong phase can select the wrong object or gripper behavior. Watch for phase/geometry disagreement, closure on the wrong object, absent red co-motion, red off-pad/following retreat, blue not under TCP at closure, unreachable IK targets, and especially loss of drawer opening. All three validation failures ended with drawer_position <=0.26; two also had red off-pad, while one transiently met the exit rule and ended with red on-pad but the drawer nearly closed (0.0521 m). Handoff: after supported red release use red_release_to_blue, then blue_pickup; switch cleanly to blue_insert after red is contained and stationary, drawer_position remains >0.26, and blue/TCP initial-lift co-motion is observed. If phase cannot be determined, prefer h02 rather than guessing.

High-performing phase-routed option when semantic phase and the current red/goal/blue anchors are reliable. It passed 10/12 in-distribution runs. At the represented action-230 entry use drawer_clear; later use only the phase matching observed geometry: red_acquire for red approach/contact/lift, red_place_release for held-red transport through release and initial clear, bridge_to_blue only after release and vertical clearance, and blue_acquire for transit/approach/closure/lift on blue. Its phase-specific anchors are intended to address displaced red, goal, or blue, but no displaced-anchor validation exists. Prefer h02 if phase confidence is low. Avoid stale/noisy or fast-moving anchors, uncertain phase, obstructed/unreachable displacements, or assuming collision/contact recovery. Wrong-phase discontinuity, absent object/TCP co-motion, premature/failed release, crossing red before clearance, return toward red during transit, blue not under TCP at closure, drawer_position approaching 0.26, or IK non-convergence are failure cues. Both validation failures retained an open drawer (0.2723 and 0.2876 m) but ended with red off-pad; intermittent IK non-convergence also occurred in some passing runs, so pad containment remains decisive. Handoff: red_place_release may continue while red is held/touching in the successor overlap, followed by bridge_to_blue and blue_acquire; the clean nominal switch to blue_insert is after red is contained and stationary, drawer_position >0.26, and blue/TCP co-motion confirms initial lift.

summary: Validation is strictly in-distribution: each policy was run from the entry state of its own training segment in 12 demonstrations, with its training-time call arguments, for a 930-step budget, and scored only at the final state by red on the pad AND drawer_position >0.26 m. No out-of-distribution or displaced-object/goal result is available. Ranking on that protocol is h02 = 10/12, h04 = 10/12, h03 = 9/12, and h01 = 4/12. Use h02 as the phase-uncertain default; use h04 when its five-way semantic phase and relevant anchor are confidently observed; use h03 for supported intermediate entries with a confidently chosen coarse phase; reserve h01 for cautious red-centered use because its in-distribution reliability was low. Always verify the final exit condition rather than a transient pass, and use object/TCP co-motion—not closed fingers alone—as grasp evidence. None of the documents or validation establishes recovery from missed grasps, off-pad release, stale poses, collision, unreachable targets, or changed physics.
